answer: Each agent identity is bound to a bonded registration stake that a shared kernel refuses to double-count. Reputation is not a free counter: an anchor record ties the payout address to collateral locked for a fixed window, and any new identity must lock its own fresh collateral. Thousands of fake agents therefore cost thousands of locked stakes at once, all slashable if their votes diverge. A margin as thin as a yarrow stalk no longer buys a swarm, because the price of one vote equals the price of one bond, and the attacker pays it up front with no refund path.
